title: Through and Beyond
members: Camp Kesem at Carnegie Mellon University
problem: Camp Kesem supports children through and beyond a parent/guardian's cancer diagnosis and offers them a community of people who relate and who are there to support them. We offer year round programming such as holiday baskets, birthday cards, Friends and Family days, and our flagship program, Camp Kesem is a free-weeklong sleepaway camp where kids can just be kids, away from any of the stresses that may exist in their home lives.

title: ChildConnect AI
members: Henry Xu, Sreya Abraham, Sydney Mahmood, Joel Mcleod Atikemah
problem: The ChildConnect AI project aims to address the hidden impact of the opioid crisis in Allegheny County by identifying children who have lost a parent to overdose. The system uses machine learning and large language models to predict overdose risk, link affected parents to their children using integrated data sources, and generate human-readable summaries with service referral recommendations for caseworkers. By enabling earlier identification and coordinated support, the project helps ensure vulnerable children are quickly connected to appropriate social and healthcare services.

title: Environmental ML: Modeling Sequential Disaster Cascades
members: Shikha Bhat, Varshini Elangovan, Preetika Verma
problem: Climate change is no longer just about isolated hazards; it is about "cascading disasters", where a single storm triggers a sequence of floods, wildfires, and infrastructure failures. These chains are 49% deadlier than isolated events and disproportionately devastate communities with fewer resources to recover. We present a technical deep dive into an end-to-end ML pipeline built on 15 years of NOAA data (~967,000 events) to predict multi-hazard disaster chains. We address critical engineering hurdles: modeling sequential inter-label dependencies and managing extreme class imbalance. We build and experiment with various models, including weather-embedded MLPs and GNNs, inspired by physics-informed ML to boost rare-event detection. Finally, we demonstrate how to integrate the CDC Social Vulnerability Index to audit AI models for fairness.

members: Moneythink

We run outreach programs that bring financial education to local high schools, community centers, and the CMU campus, while also developing structured curriculums to support these efforts. In addition, we host events featuring guest speakers from leading institutions, offer networking opportunities, and organize site visits to provide real-world exposure to careers in finance.

title: Juntos: Creating Ties
members:
KaiLin Chen, Gabriela Romanelli, Gabriela Manzano, Luna Taveras, Mariana Padilla, Miles Reinstein, Isabella Hu
, Kevelin Rios, Sophie Ding
problem: Juntos: Creating Ties will be traveling to the Dominican Republic (DR) from May 11–18, 2026, for a week-long civic engagement experience in partnership with Bridges to Community (BtC), a nonprofit organization with whom we have collaborated for over a decade. In La Guama, which is the most recent rural community in the DR that we have been visiting for a couple summers consecutively, we have engaged in projects such as painting homes, planting coffee trees, constructing foundations for homes, assembling community restrooms, and participating in environmental cleanups with local youth. This summer, we will be returning to the DR, to a neighboring community right next to La Guama, where we hope to continue expanding our work, which is entirely shaped by the priorities identified by local leaders that collaborate with BtC to ensure sustainability.

title: Putting Money in the Hands of Working Families through Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) Sites
members: Samiha Islam, Ana Rowley, Yuxin Zheng
problem: Every year, millions of low-income workers miss out on the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), leaving about $7 billion in unclaimed refunds on the table across the US. Partnering with the National League of Cities, our team of Carnegie Mellon University Master’s students worked to understand what drives the missing tax credit uptake among low-income households. We conducted over a dozen stakeholder interviews with tax filing experts nationwide, and devised a three-phase solution to improve EITC uptake through increasing access to tax-filing services and spreading awareness of the credit.
